theorem_title: Elements algebraic over K[x] generate an algebra of transcendence degree at most one
formal_statement:
namespace Transcendence

theorem trdeg_adjoin_le_one_of_isAlgebraic_adjoin {K L : Type*} [Field K] [Field L]
    [Algebra K L] (x : L) (S : Set L)
    (hS : ∀ s ∈ S, IsAlgebraic ↥(Algebra.adjoin K ({x} : Set L)) s) :
    Algebra.trdeg K ↥(Algebra.adjoin K S) ≤ 1 := by
  sorry

end Transcendence
natural_language_statement:
Let $K \subseteq L$ be fields, let $x \in L$, and let $S \subseteq L$ be a set each of whose elements is algebraic over the ring $K[x]$. Then the $K$-algebra $K[S]$ generated by $S$ has transcendence degree at most one over $K$.

The element $x$ need not belong to $S$. This is the form in which a transcendence-degree hypothesis is usually checked: one generator at a time, each shown to be algebraic over $K[x]$ for a single $x$. In the Diaz modulus mission the same argument had been repeated inside fourteen proofs before it was published as a node of its own.
source: Standard. Formal proof: Diaz modulus mission, 24 September 2026 (C. Perassi).
